https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eshtemoa.findingJa: Article identifies Eshtemoa as ancient city in southern Hebron Hills, identified with As-Samu’, and notes separate individuals with same name in Chronicles. It supports 1 Samuel 30:28 city identity.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geba_(city.findingJa: Identifies a biblical city and distinguishes Geba from Gibeah and Gibeon.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebron.findingJa: Article concerns modern Hebron and ancient city history, including the older name Kiryath-arba and ancient Tel Rumeida. Modern city and ancient urban core/sacred site should not be collapsed into one point.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baal-hazor.findingJa: Calls Baal-hazor an ancient village at the Ephraim/Benjamin border; directly cites 2 Samuel 13:23 and proposes Tell Asur. Related identity support, not coordinate verification.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahurim.findingJa: Calls Bahurim a village east of Jerusalem; describes Paltiel returning after Michal was brought to David and later Shimei/messengers/Azmaveth references. Several competing site proposals; no single identification secure.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeroth_(b.findingJa: Explicitly cites 2 Samuel 4:2–3; says location is disputed and gives competing site proposals.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berothah.findingJa: Says Berothah is probably identified with Berothai, and gives a probable modern site; preserves uncertainty.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo-debar.findingJa: Identifies a town in Gilead near Mahanaim and Jabbok; cites 2 Samuel 9:4–5.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazer.findingJa: Identifies Jazer east of Jordan, in or near Gilead, and notes surrounding territory bearing the name; this excerpt does not prove the Samuel census use or exact point.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuph.findingJa: Distinguishes ancestor Zuph from “land of Zuph” in the Samuel narrative; relevant to a land-region reading, not a fixed point.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeboim_(He.findingJa: Distinguishes Valley of Zeboyim near Gibeah in Benjamin (1 Samuel 13:18) from the separate Zeboim in Nehemiah; Wadi Shaykh ad-Dub’a is tentative.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_(ancie.findingJa: Covers the northern ancient city/Tel Dan and tribe; the “Dan to Beersheba” formula is distinct and does not identify the city as an occurrence.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geba_(city.findingJa: Identifies a biblical city and distinguishes Geba from Gibeah and Gibeon.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giloh.findingJa: Identifies Judahite Giloh and says Ahitophel came from Giloh; distinguishes from modern Gilo.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hama.findingJa: “Hamath in the Bible” section cites the king of Hamath congratulating David after Hadadezer defeat (2 Samuel 8:9–11).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizpah_(Mo.findingJa: Says David moved his parents to Mizpah in Moab (1 Samuel 22:3); several modern locations are proposed.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mi.findingJa: Exact Perez Uzzah entry names the place after Uzzah and says location unknown; exact Racal/Rachal/Rakal entry says site unknown and possible copyist error.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzzah.findingJa: Article concerns Uzzah the person and the place Perez-uzzah named in his death narrative; related-person context, not a location profile.
